clue.text: Keen to enter points and win lottery

indicators.note: one piece going to enter another means it sits inside it

parts.note: two compass points, south and south again
to keen is to wail or weep
to take a prize or game is to win it

explanation.surface: Someone eager to score points and win the lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager, but it is the verb to wail.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a form of gambling lottery where the stakes go to the winners.

clue.text: Letter from Athens dismissing tour leader in disgrace

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace

indicators.note: the leader of the word tour is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Greek letter dismisses the tour leader who is in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Financial expert's scam only initially in Times, oddly

indicators.note: the scam and the initial go in the rearranged letters
oddly says the letters of Times are mixed up

parts.note: a con is a scam or swindle

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of only

explanation.surface: A financial expert's swindle appears in The Times, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' reorders TIMES as E MIST, and CON plus O go inside after the E; the 's of expert's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An economist studies money, markets and the economy.

clue.text: Emergency touchdown after a toss-up?

parts.note: an aircraft belly-flop that drops flat, pictured as what follows tossing a batter disc in a pan

explanation.surface: A forced landing after a coin toss.
explanation.definitionFit: A pancake landing is an aircraft dropping flat onto the ground in an emergency.

clue.text: Army commander accepting mixed-up type on a course

indicators.note: the army commander pair accepts the type between them

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army
OC is Officer Commanding
pi is printers' term for jumbled type

explanation.surface: An army commander takes on some muddled recruit on a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed-up type' is printers' pi; 'accepting' sets it inside the army commander pair. 'course' is a pudding course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starchy pudding, served as a dessert course.

clue.text: Knight restrains monster renouncing current parliament

indicators.note: the knight restrains the monster by holding it inside
renouncing means giving up, so a letter goes

parts.note: Nessie is the Loch Ness monster
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A knight holds back a monster that has given up the present parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renouncing' takes I from the monster's name, leaving NESSE; 'restrains' holds that inside the knight's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Knesset is the national legislature of Israel.

clue.text: Knocked back drink after start of office work

indicators.note: the drink comes after the office letter
the start of the word office is its first letter
knocked back is read as turned round, so the drink word goes backwards

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A worker downs a drink after arriving at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests swallowing a drink, but here it reverses the drink word to give PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work, especially a numbered composition.

clue.text: Report of military detachment showing a little bottle

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is spoken

parts.note: a file is a line of soldiers

explanation.surface: A report of troops showing a small bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass vial for medicines or liquids.

clue.text: Having broken desk, go off to get bolt

indicators.note: having broken the desk means its letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: eggs addle when they go off, turning rotten

explanation.surface: Having smashed a desk, someone goes off to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is to run away, to bolt or scarper.

clue.text: Less sensitive eater's computer

parts.note: more numb is less sensitive
a cruncher is someone who crunches food, an eater

explanation.surface: A less sensitive eater's computer.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is read as the comparative of numb, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A number cruncher is a computer, or person, doing large calculations.

clue.text: Mature Republican wearing academic dress at university

indicators.note: the Republican is wearing the gown, so the gown goes round it

parts.note: a gown is worn by academics
being up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: A grown-up Republican student dons a gown at college.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is an adult, someone fully mature.

clue.text: Learned European uncivil about wine

indicators.note: the uncivil word goes about the wine, enclosing it

parts.note: uncivil means rude
IT is short for Italian vermouth, a crossword wine

explanation.surface: A clever European is rude about the wine served.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite is a synonym for scholarly, having much book learning.

clue.text: Atypical soul, somehow, with a lack of qualification

parts.note: no means none, a lack of
MA, Master of Arts, is an academic qualification

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of soul are rearranged in some fashion

explanation.surface: An unusual soul gets by somehow without any qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the letters of soul into LOUS, which ends the answer; 'a lack of qualification' reads as A, NO, MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomalous means irregular or deviating from the norm, a synonym of atypical.

clue.text: Lake accommodating sailor's first light raft

indicators.note: the lake accommodates the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Bala is a lake in North Wales

indicators.note: the first letter of sailor

explanation.surface: A lake where a sailor first launches a light raft.
explanation.walkthrough: Bala Lake (Llyn Tegid) is the largest natural lake in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light wood, and the word also names a raft or float made from it.

clue.text: Gangster and president possessing similar characteristics

parts.note: Al Capone was the famous gangster
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A gangster and a president turn out to have a lot in common.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are alike resemble each other closely in their features.

clue.text: Record-keeper this vicar could become

indicators.note: could become says these letters may be rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A vicar could become the parish record-keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: An archivist looks after historical records and documents.

clue.text: Non-university man joins old school as worker, perhaps

indicators.note: without university removes U, the abbreviation for university

parts.note: Arthur is a man's name
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A man who never went to university joins an old school as a worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is a worker ant, which is an example of the definition: the 'perhaps' signals that.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker ant is an insect, and insects belong to the phylum of jointed-legged invertebrates.

clue.text: Musical sergeant addicted to Italian capital's spicy food

parts.note: Sgt Pepper is the sergeant of the Beatles album
being on a drug is being addicted to it

indicators.note: the capital letter of Italian is its first

explanation.surface: A musical sergeant hooked on Italian capital's spicy food.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy Italian-style salami sausage.

clue.text: Accountants embrace his art, oddly, for relief of tensions

indicators.note: the accountants embrace the other letters, surrounding them

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant, so CAs are accountants

indicators.note: oddly says the letters of his art are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: Accountants find release from stress in his art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' turns HIS ART into THARSI, which sits between C A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is the purging or release of pent-up emotion, bringing relief.

clue.text: Leader in rebellion replaces article in Italian port

indicators.note: replaces means one piece takes the place of another

parts.note: San Remo is a resort port on the Italian Riviera
an is the indefinite article
a rising up is a rebellion

explanation.surface: A rebel leader replaces an article in an Italian port.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is a person in overall charge, a leader or boss.

clue.text: Prize for Kentishman heading for coast?

parts.note: Kent is in the South East of England, so a man from there is SE
an award is a prize

explanation.surface: A prize for a man from Kent who is off to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South East England; 'Prize for Kentishman' reads as an AWARD given to an SE man.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaward means moving towards the sea, heading for the shore.

clue.text: Regret including exercise for 100 paise

indicators.note: the regret word includes the exercise inside it

parts.note: to rue is to regret
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having to exercise for a hundred small coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian currency unit is divided into a hundred smaller coins called paise.

clue.text: Work domestics rejected, lacking directions

indicators.note: rejected is read as sent back, so the trimmed word is turned round
lacking means the directions are taken away

parts.note: dailies are daily cleaning women, domestic helps
E and S, east and south, are compass directions

explanation.surface: Household staff turn down a job, having lost their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes E and S from DAILIES to leave DAILI; 'rejected' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem is a classic literary work.

clue.text: In staging Othello this must be cast

indicators.note: In says the word is found inside the following words

explanation.surface: An actor must be cast in a production of Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks theatrical, but it means poured molten into a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of metal formed by casting in a mould.

clue.text: Homely appearance of retired nurse once visiting prairies

indicators.note: the nurse is visiting, so goes inside the prairies

parts.note: prairies are grassy plains

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the nurse's letters go backwards

parts.note: SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, was a former British nursing grade

explanation.surface: A retired nurse visits the prairies and finds plain living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the old nursing grade into NES, and 'visiting' puts that inside the prairies.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainness means lack of beauty, and homely in US use means unattractive.

clue.text: Strindberg, for example, made one in the Home Counties

indicators.note: the married word goes in the area abbreviation

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
to wed is to make two into one

explanation.surface: Strindberg got married in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: August Strindberg was a Swedish playwright, a national of Sweden.

clue.text: Info used regularly by popular young actress

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of used

explanation.surface: Information is regularly passed to a popular young actress.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent young woman, especially such a role played by an actress.

clue.text: Unaccompanied going round half of this Irish town

indicators.note: the alone word goes round the half word, enclosing it

parts.note: unaccompanied means alone

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word this is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Travelling alone round an Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Athlone is a town in the Irish midlands on the River Shannon.

clue.text: Film director — surely not one associated with rubbish?

parts.note: tat is rubbish, cheap tasteless goods
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A film director is surely not someone linked with junk?
explanation.walkthrough: 'one associated with rubbish' puts I after TAT; 'surely not' adds the joke that he is far from tatty.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati was a French filmmaker, maker of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday.

clue.text: Marginal note introducing amenity for shoppers

indicators.note: the note introduces, comes in front of, the rest

parts.note: B is a musical note
an order line is a telephone line for placing orders

explanation.surface: A note mentions a new ordering service for customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Borderline describes a case on the margin between two categories.
